editorial: You follow Oliver Tate, a sharp but awkward Welsh teen who narrates his life like a movie. He wants to date Jordana, a tough classmate, while his parents' marriage cracks under quiet tension. The film mixes dry humor with teenage panic, so you get laughs and ache at the same time. It feels small, personal, and very human. The acting feels natural, the camera work is stylish without showing off, and the pacing keeps you moving from one awkward moment to the next. Some jokes are dry and the mood can feel sad, so it is not a light rom-com for every night. Watch if you like coming-of-age stories with bite and honesty. It rewards patience and gives you a teen hero who is smart but still makes bad choices. Stream in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent on Apple TV, or buy the 4K Blu-ray.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Oliver cannot fix his parents' marriage or fully win Jordana back after her family health scare. He stops trying to control everything and accepts that people change. The last walk with Jordana suggests a possible fresh start, but nothing is neatly solved, leaving you with hope instead of a fairy-tale ending.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves awkward teen stories with dry humor and heart.
similarMovies: The Perks of Being a Wallflower
